Each section below follows the same pattern: **run the function → get a logical vector → subset to the TRUE results → map what was actually selected**. This is the workflow you'd use in a real analysis.

## Setup


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(sf)
library(tmap)
library(tidyverse)
```
:::


### Greenway Park and its neighbors


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Reference: Greenway Park — a 10×10 city block
park <- st_sf(name = "Park",
              geometry = st_as_sfc("POLYGON((0 0, 10 0, 10 10, 0 10, 0 0))"))

# Completely inside the park, no shared boundary edges
garden <- st_sf(name = "Garden",
                geometry = st_as_sfc("POLYGON((2 2, 8 2, 8 8, 2 8, 2 2))"))

# Interior inside the park, but its left and bottom edges lie on the park's boundary
courtyard <- st_sf(name = "Courtyard",
                   geometry = st_as_sfc("POLYGON((0 0, 5 0, 5 5, 0 5, 0 0))"))

# Just east — shares only the park's right edge (x = 10), interiors never overlap
plaza <- st_sf(name = "Plaza",
               geometry = st_as_sfc("POLYGON((10 0, 18 0, 18 10, 10 10, 10 0))"))

# Encroaches into the park's NE corner
development <- st_sf(name = "Development",
                     geometry = st_as_sfc("POLYGON((5 5, 16 5, 16 16, 5 16, 5 5))"))

# No contact with the park at all
vacant_lot <- st_sf(name = "Vacant Lot",
                    geometry = st_as_sfc("POLYGON((12 2, 18 2, 18 8, 12 8, 12 2))"))

# Point features
fountain <- st_sf(name = "Fountain", geometry = st_as_sfc("POINT(5 5)"))   # inside
gate     <- st_sf(name = "Gate",     geometry = st_as_sfc("POINT(10 5)"))  # on east boundary
bus_stop <- st_sf(name = "Bus Stop", geometry = st_as_sfc("POINT(14 5)")) # outside

polys <- bind_rows(garden, courtyard, plaza, development, vacant_lot)
pts   <- bind_rows(fountain, gate, bus_stop)
```
:::


### Overview


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="true"}
tm_shape(park) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "#a8d8ea", col = "#1f4e79", lwd = 2) +
tm_shape(polys) +
  tm_polygons(fill = NA, col = "gray40", lwd = 1.2, lty = "dashed") +
  tm_text("name", size = 0.7) +
tm_shape(pts) +
  tm_dots(fill = "#6a1b9a", size = 0.6) +
  tm_text("name", size = 0.65, ymod = 0.8) +
tm_title("Greenway District") +
tm_layout(inner.margins = 0.15)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](topological_relationships_files/figure-html/overview-map-1.png){width=864}
:::
:::


---

## Visualization helper

Each map below shows **all features in gray for context**, then **highlights the subset that returned TRUE** in green.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Show all polys as context (gray) and highlight those that returned TRUE (green)
plot_selected <- function(selected, title) {
  tm_shape(polys) +
    tm_polygons(fill = "gray92", col = "gray60", lwd = 0.8) +
  tm_shape(park) +
    tm_polygons(fill = "#a8d8ea", col = "#1f4e79", lwd = 1.5) +
  tm_shape(selected) +
    tm_polygons(fill = "#b7e4c7", col = "#1b4332", lwd = 1.5) +
    tm_text("name", size = 0.7) +
  tm_title(title) +
  tm_layout(inner.margins = 0.12)
}
```
:::


---

## `st_intersects()` — any spatial contact at all {#intersects}

Returns `TRUE` whenever two features share **any** geometry — even a single boundary point.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Run the function — 1 row (park) × 5 cols (polys) logical matrix
result <- st_intersects(park, polys, sparse = FALSE)
result
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
     [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]  [,5]
[1,] TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE FALSE
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# Subset to features that returned TRUE
polys[result[1, ], ]$name
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Garden"      "Courtyard"   "Plaza"       "Development"
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_selected(polys[result[1, ], ], "st_intersects(park, ?) — selected features")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](topological_relationships_files/figure-html/intersects-map-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


Four out of five features share some geometry with the park. Only the **vacant lot** returns `FALSE`.

---

## `st_disjoint()` — no contact whatsoever {#disjoint}

The exact complement of `st_intersects()`. Returns `TRUE` only when two features share **nothing** — no interior, no boundary.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
result <- st_disjoint(park, polys, sparse = FALSE)
result
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
      [,1]  [,2]  [,3]  [,4] [,5]
[1,] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
polys[result[1, ], ]$name
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Vacant Lot"
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_selected(polys[result[1, ], ], "st_disjoint(park, ?) — selected features")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](topological_relationships_files/figure-html/disjoint-map-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


---

## `st_touches()` — boundary contact, interiors stay separate {#touches}

Returns `TRUE` when features share **boundary points** but their **interiors do not intersect**. Think of two adjacent floor tiles sharing an edge but not overlapping.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
result <- st_touches(park, polys, sparse = FALSE)
result
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
      [,1]  [,2] [,3]  [,4]  [,5]
[1,] FALSE FALSE TRUE FALSE FALSE
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
polys[result[1, ], ]$name
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Plaza"
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_selected(polys[result[1, ], ], "st_touches(park, ?) — selected features")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](topological_relationships_files/figure-html/touches-map-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


::: {.callout-important}
### The courtyard result

The courtyard shares **two full edges** with the park boundary, but `st_touches` returned `FALSE` for it. Why?

`st_touches` requires that the **interiors do not intersect**. The courtyard's interior sits inside the park's interior — so the relationship is *more than* touching. Even though their boundaries meet, their interiors also overlap, which disqualifies it. Only the **plaza**, whose interior remains entirely outside the park while sharing one boundary edge, satisfies `st_touches()`.
:::

---

## `st_overlaps()` — partial interior overlap {#overlaps}

Returns `TRUE` when two features share **some interior** without either fully containing the other.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
result <- st_overlaps(park, polys, sparse = FALSE)
result
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
      [,1]  [,2]  [,3] [,4]  [,5]
[1,] FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE FALSE
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
polys[result[1, ], ]$name
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Development"
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_selected(polys[result[1, ], ], "st_overlaps(park, ?) — selected features")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](topological_relationships_files/figure-html/overlaps-map-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


Only the **development** qualifies — it encroaches into the park without being fully contained by it. The garden and courtyard fail because the park completely contains them; overlaps requires neither fully contain the other.

---

## `st_contains()` and `st_within()` — an inverse pair {#contains-within}

`st_contains(park, polys)` and `st_within(polys, park)` ask the same spatial question from opposite directions. Compare the result matrix dimensions: one is `1×5`, the other is `5×1`.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# st_contains(park, polys): 1 row (park) × 5 cols (polys)
contains_result <- st_contains(park, polys, sparse = FALSE)
contains_result
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
     [,1] [,2]  [,3]  [,4]  [,5]
[1,] TRUE TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
polys[contains_result[1, ], ]$name
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Garden"    "Courtyard"
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# st_within(polys, park): 5 rows (polys) × 1 col (park)
within_result <- st_within(polys, park, sparse = FALSE)
within_result
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
      [,1]
[1,]  TRUE
[2,]  TRUE
[3,] FALSE
[4,] FALSE
[5,] FALSE
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
polys[within_result[, 1], ]$name
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Garden"    "Courtyard"
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_selected(polys[contains_result[1, ], ], "st_contains(park, ?) — same result as st_within(?, park)")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](topological_relationships_files/figure-html/contains-map-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


Both return `TRUE` for the same two features. Note that the **courtyard** counts even though it shares edges with the park boundary — being on the boundary still qualifies as being within.

---

## `st_contains()` vs `st_contains_properly()` — does the boundary matter? {#contains-properly}

Both ask "does the park fully hold this feature?" but they disagree when a feature's boundary **touches** the park's boundary. Subset each and compare what's selected.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# st_contains: feature may sit on the park boundary
contains_result  <- st_contains(park, polys, sparse = FALSE)

# st_contains_properly: feature must lie entirely in the park's INTERIOR
properly_result  <- st_contains_properly(park, polys, sparse = FALSE)

# What each selects
polys[contains_result[1, ], ]$name
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Garden"    "Courtyard"
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
polys[properly_result[1, ], ]$name
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Garden"
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tmap_arrange(
  plot_selected(polys[contains_result[1, ], ],  "st_contains — selects both"),
  plot_selected(polys[properly_result[1, ], ],  "st_contains_properly — drops courtyard"),
  ncol = 2
)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](topological_relationships_files/figure-html/contains-properly-map-1.png){width=1152}
:::
:::


The **courtyard** is the only difference: `st_contains` keeps it (no part extends outside the park), `st_contains_properly` drops it (two edges touch the park boundary).

::: {.callout-tip icon=true}
### When does this matter?

If two adjacent polygons share a boundary, a feature sitting exactly on that border would be "contained" by both under `st_contains()`. Use `st_contains_properly()` to avoid double-counting those boundary features.
:::

---

## `st_covers()` vs `st_contains()` — the point-on-boundary edge case {#covers-contains}

For polygon–polygon comparisons these two functions select the same features. The difference only appears when testing **points sitting exactly on a polygon's boundary**.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
contains_pts <- st_contains(park, pts, sparse = FALSE)
covers_pts   <- st_covers(park, pts, sparse = FALSE)

# What each selects
pts[contains_pts[1, ], ]$name
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Fountain"
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
pts[covers_pts[1, ], ]$name
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Fountain" "Gate"    
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="true"}
plot_pts_selected <- function(selected, title) {
  tm_shape(park) +
    tm_polygons(fill = "#a8d8ea", col = "#1f4e79", lwd = 1.5) +
  tm_shape(pts) +
    tm_dots(fill = "gray60", size = 0.8) +
  tm_shape(selected) +
    tm_dots(fill = "#1b4332", size = 1.5) +
    tm_text("name", size = 0.7, ymod = 0.8) +
  tm_title(title) +
  tm_layout(inner.margins = 0.12)
}

tmap_arrange(
  plot_pts_selected(pts[contains_pts[1, ], ], "st_contains — fountain only"),
  plot_pts_selected(pts[covers_pts[1, ], ],   "st_covers — fountain + gate"),
  ncol = 2
)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](topological_relationships_files/figure-html/covers-map-1.png){width=1152}
:::
:::


The **gate** is the only difference. It sits exactly on the park's east edge (x = 10):

- `st_contains` returns `FALSE` — the boundary is not the interior
- `st_covers` returns `TRUE` — nothing in the gate is *outside* the park

The same logic reversed:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# st_within vs st_covered_by — gate is on the boundary
st_within(    gate, park, sparse = FALSE)    # FALSE
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
      [,1]
[1,] FALSE
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
st_covered_by(gate, park, sparse = FALSE)    # TRUE
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
     [,1]
[1,] TRUE
```


:::
:::


::: {.callout-tip icon=true}
`st_covers()` / `st_covered_by()` are more permissive — they include boundary points. For polygon–polygon filtering the two pairs behave identically; the distinction only matters for points or lines sitting on a polygon boundary.
:::

---

## Summary


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Feature     |st_intersects |st_disjoint |st_touches |st_overlaps |st_contains |st_contains_properly |st_covers |st_within |
|:-----------|:-------------|:-----------|:----------|:-----------|:-----------|:--------------------|:---------|:---------|
|Garden      |TRUE          |FALSE       |FALSE      |FALSE       |TRUE        |TRUE                 |TRUE      |TRUE      |
|Courtyard   |TRUE          |FALSE       |FALSE      |FALSE       |TRUE        |FALSE                |TRUE      |TRUE      |
|Plaza       |TRUE          |FALSE       |TRUE       |FALSE       |FALSE       |FALSE                |FALSE     |FALSE     |
|Development |TRUE          |FALSE       |FALSE      |TRUE        |FALSE       |FALSE                |FALSE     |FALSE     |
|Vacant Lot  |FALSE         |TRUE        |FALSE      |FALSE       |FALSE       |FALSE                |FALSE     |FALSE     |


:::
:::


::: {.callout-note icon=true}
### Key pairs

| Pair | Distinction |
|---|---|
| `st_intersects` / `st_disjoint` | Exact complements |
| `st_touches` / `st_overlaps` | Touches = boundary only; overlaps = shared interior, neither contains the other |
| `st_contains` / `st_within` | Same test, argument order reversed — matrix transposes |
| `st_contains` / `st_contains_properly` | `contains_properly` drops features that touch the boundary |
| `st_covers` / `st_contains` | `covers` includes boundary points; only differs for points/lines on a boundary |
:::
